questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted a personal challenge and to try something completely different from studying in Denmark while still improving my academic skills.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have visited Australia before, and I really wanted to go back to Sydney. Important to me was to find a place where I could feel safe, a place where I couldn't just go back to visit my friends and family for safety, and a place from where I could travel to cool destinations and enjoy the city I lived in. Sydney and Australia has so much to offer!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university website was really informative, and the university is really good at reaching out and giving the information you need as an exchange student.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The website of the university and emails from the university, along with a webinar before our travel and an "Exchange Orientation" meeting at arrival and other fun activities where the exchange students got to meet each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university had its own housing, but everything was full. Furthermore, there was a private student housing opportunity called "Macquarie Village", and then two colleges; "Dunmore Lang College" and "Robert Menzies College" (where I stayed).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Robert Menzies offered meal plans. You could be self catered, semi catered (my option - 5 meals a week) or fully catered.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I thought it was great to live on campus, because I was close to the university where we had a good library to study in. However, best of all was the college life where I really felt like a part of a society. We had so much fun together, and everyone helped each other. This took my exchange experience to a new level! Exchange students before me have said that it was too far from the city center, but the university has its own metro stop, so the transport from uni to Town Hall was 30 minutes which was absolutely fine. At day, the metro and trains go all the time, and at night, there are busses from the city center to the university every 30-40 minutes. I enjoyed this a lot, and I spent a lot of time in the city and going to clubs at night as well - the transport was never an issue.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To register for the units, the university had a system/website to go through. They had introduction text and videos, so it was easy to do. The only negative thing to point out is that you cannot see the time tables beforehand, so I had to choose another unit, because my classes clashed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university website, the unit guide, YouTube videos, and the registrations process was also described in the introduction webinar and in introduction emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I only had to change one unit registration, because the class clashed with another unit. However, you can change your units even after classes have started which is so cool and makes it less stressful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check out the unit guide and the Macquarie web site. Take it easy and read the emails from the university. You can always ask the nice staff to help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fine. Some units were easier than others. The "international" law units were easier because you do not need to have knowledge of the Australian common law system. I found that the unit "Remedies" was much harder than expected, as I was missing a lot of background information.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Your final grade is not your exam alone. You get grades for participation and assignments along the way. This made it easier and made the exam less stressful. We had online pre recorded lectures in most units, and then we had tutorials which was teaching in smaller groups. The teaching was good, and I learned a lot from showing up to classes. There is a lot of reading, but it is not all required, so you should be good at distinguish the important readings from the less important readings.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LAWS8015 - International Law 
LAWS8098 - International Commercial Law
LAWS8030 - The Law of Obligations I - Contracts 
LAWS8027 - Law of Obligations III - Remedies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend units about different types of international law. This can be useful in Denmark as well, and it is easier to follow. However, I also enjoyed contract law, and this was fairly easy to follow as well. I would not recommend Remedies, as a lot of background information about the Australian law system is required. Most important is to go with what you find interesting!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Comment about the insurance: A required Overseas Health Cover (1.600 DKK) plus my personal travel insurance which covered many things, because I also travelled Australia before and after my exchange period.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is generally really expensive to live in Sydney. Housing and alcohol is especially more expensive than in Denmark. On the other hand, good barista coffee is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of clubs of every kind! You can check out the Macquarie website, where the clubs are listed.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You can most definitely find activities you would enjoy. There are lots of clubs - athletic, cultural, political and social. I enjoyed the Sport and Aquatic Center at the university (where I got a free membership through my college). In general, I also just enjoyed going to the city as a tourist and traveling Australia as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the many different places in Sydney - beautiful beaches, great architecture and a lot of amazing experiences. I especially loved The Rocks (and the markets there every weekend), Circular Quay, Darling Harbour and Manly Beach. But check out all of Sydney! There is a lot of free experiences, including free entry to every museum. Enjoy the bars and restaurants as well - I spent a lot of time with friends at different locations around the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - it is very impacted by the "western culture". However, I loved the multicultural Sydney, where people come from all around the world, so there is a lot to learn about different cultures.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be outgoing and be yourself. You'll come a long way being interested in other people and always being open minded. Everyone is so friendly, and it is easy to make new friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are friendly and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Show up to classes and participate - you will get easy marks that way and you will understand a lot more and not lose yourself in all the readings. 

Enjoy the university and everything it has to offer. 

Also remember to get out of campus and go to the city center quite often - it has so much to offer!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know new people from around the world and figuring out how easy it is to make new friends, when you are curious about people and open minded.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Everything you need to sort out before the exchange can be exhausting, but it is all worth it, and you forget about it, when you are there and just enjoying life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
